main_topics.reason: User opened with six months of severe pelvic pain that sometimes stops them working and returned to wanting the pain treated now.
User repeatedly said the doctor calls it normal cramps and does not believe them, and asked how to get tests if not believed.
User explained SUS has no insurance network, months-long waits for a gynecologist, and was frustrated the bot kept suggesting insurance.
User mentioned a possible endometriosis diagnosis and the bot covered diagnostic steps, but it was context for the pain and access problems.
User asked for treatment now and took up the continuous pill idea to ask their doctor about over a few turns.
User asked once how to get an ultrasound if the doctor does not believe them.
User said in one line that they sometimes cannot work because of the pain.
User expressed feeling unbelieved and growing frustration, ending with 'this is not helping me'.
User briefly said the diary was maybe ok but did not engage further.

output.summary: A user in Brazil using the public system (SUS) described six months of severe pelvic pain, a doctor who calls it normal cramps, and suspected endometriosis. The bot repeatedly advised insurance referrals, in-network directories and US-style telehealth despite the user explaining several times that this does not apply in Brazil. The user got one useful idea, asking about a continuous contraceptive pill, but still could not see a way to a specialist and left saying the chat was not helping.
